extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examiners on applying 35 U.S.C. 102(e)/103(a) to copending applications and on restriction/double patenting practice (distinctness, genus/species, combination/subcombination, process/apparatus).

rubrics_metrics.name: 102(e) prior-art from copending applications with common assignee/inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: A copending application with an earlier filing date that discloses the claimed invention (but has not been published under 35 U.S.C. 122) constitutes prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) if the copending application has either a common assignee or at least one common inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph guidance (e.g., 7.12/7.12.01/7.15.02). This rejection may be overcome by a showing under 37 CFR 1.132 that any invention disclosed but not claimed in the reference was derived from the inventor of this application (thus not 'by another') or by an appropriate showing under 37 CFR 1.131. Insert appropriate bracket language (e.g., --assignee-- or --inventor-- in bracket 3). See Examiner Notes for further application rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of 35 U.S.C. 102(e) effective date (AIPA vs pre-AIPA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 35 U.S.C. 102(e) as amended by the American Inventors Protection Act (AIPA) and IP/High-Tech Technical Amendments to determine the copending application's prior art date, unless the copending application is based (directly or indirectly) on an international application having an international filing date prior to November 29, 2000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the copending reference is a national stage of an international application or a continuing application claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120/121/365(c) to an international application with an international filing date prior to Nov. 29, 2000, use pre-AIPA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) (form paragraph 7.12.01). See Examiner Notes for form paragraphs 7.12 and 7.12.01 to determine the 102(e) date; consider priority/benefit claims under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), 120, 121, 365(c) only when the relied-upon earlier application appropriately supports the subject matter used for the rejection. Do NOT consider foreign priority claims under 119(a)-(d) and 365(a) for the 102(e) date.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a publication of an international application is NOT 102(e) prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reference is a publication of an international application (including voluntary U.S. publication under 35 U.S.C. 122 of the national stage or a WIPO publication) that has an international filing date prior to November 29, 2000, did not designate the United States or was not published in English by WIPO, the reference is not prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a reference may be applied under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or (b) as of its publication date (see form paragraphs 7.08 and 7.09). Do not use the 102(e) form paragraph in these circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overcoming 102(e)/103 rejections involving copending applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A rejection based on a copending application may be overcome by: (1) a showing under 37 CFR 1.132 that the invention disclosed but not claimed in the reference was derived from the inventor of this application; (2) a showing of an earlier date of invention for the instant application under 37 CFR 1.131; or (3) where applicable, an oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.130 that the application and reference are commonly owned and the inventor is prior, together with a terminal disclaimer under 37 CFR 1.321(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also possible: show that the copending application is disqualified as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 103(c). For provisional 103(a) rejections, the rejection is a presumption of future publication/patenting of the copending application; annotate bracketed explanation of obviousness when using provisional form paragraphs (e.g., 7.21.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103(a) for copending application
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims may be provisionally rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as being obvious over a copending application which has a common assignee or at least one common inventor, based on the earlier effective U.S. filing date of the copending application and a presumption of its future publication or patenting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.21.01 for provisional rejections; include explanation of obviousness in bracket 4. This provisional rejection should not be used where the copending application is disqualified under 35 U.S.C. 103(c) (see MPEP §706.02(l)(3)). If claimed invention is also claimed in the copending application, also give provisional obviousness double patenting rejection using paragraphs 8.33 and 8.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraphs and required bracket insertions
rubrics_metrics.description: When using form paragraphs (e.g., 7.15.02, 7.21.01, 7.21.02), include the appropriate bracket insertions (e.g., claim number, reference, --assignee-- or --inventor--, and explanation of obviousness or particulars supporting findings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Notes accompanying form paragraphs specify what to insert in each bracket and when the paragraph should or should not be used (e.g., preceding paragraphs 7.12 or 7.12.01 required for 7.15.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission to Technology Center Director for double patenting relying on parent restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Office action containing a rejection on the ground of double patenting that relies on the parent application rejecting the claims in a divisional or continuing application filed because of a restriction under 35 U.S.C. 121 (including an election of species) must be submitted to the Technology Center Director for approval prior to mailing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Director disapproves the double patenting rejection, it shall not be mailed and other appropriate action shall be taken. See MPEP §1003. Note also that where restriction is required by the Office, double patenting cannot be held (35 U.S.C. 121).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable number of species linked by an allowable generic claim (37 CFR 1.141)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.141 provides that an allowable generic claim may link a reasonable number of species embraced thereby; the examiner may require election of species if application contains claims to more than a reasonable number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice is set forth in 37 CFR 1.146. First action may require election of a species if no genus claim is allowable; examiner may require restriction to not more than a reasonable number of species before further action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare claimed subject matter to determine distinctness/independence
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining double patenting and restriction questions, it is the claimed subject matter that is considered and must be compared to determine distinctness or independence of alleged inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General principles: (A) If inventions are independent (no disclosed relation), restriction to one is ordinarily proper. (B) If inventions are related as disclosed but distinct as claimed, restriction may be proper. (C) If inventions are related as disclosed and not distinct as claimed, restriction is never proper. See MPEP §806.01 and §802.01 for criteria for patentably distinct inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single disclosed embodiment with claims defining same essential features
rubrics_metrics.description: Where claims define the same essential characteristics of a single disclosed embodiment, restriction between such claims should never be required because the claims are different definitions of the same disclosed subject matter, not distinct inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such claims are voluntarily presented in different applications with common inventor/assignee, see MPEP §804-804.02 for guidance. Rejoinder practice applies when generic claim becomes allowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species may be independent or related (genus/species analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Species under a claimed genus may be independent (not connected in design, operation, or effect under the disclosure) or related; if independent, restriction between species may be proper; if related, restriction analysis must consider both election-of-species practice and other restriction practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If species are related (e.g., intermediate and final products), distinctness must be shown (no overlap in scope, not obvious variants, and intermediate product useful other than to make final product) to sustain restriction. See MPEP §806.04(b) and §806.05(j).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and characteristics of a generic claim
rubrics_metrics.description: A generic claim should read on each illustrated species and generally require no material element additional to those required by the species claims; each species claim must require all limitations of the generic claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once a generic claim is allowable, species claims that require all limitations of the generic claim will ordinarily be allowable; when species claims do not require all generic limitations, see MPEP §821.04(a). Rejoinder of previously non-elected species may be required when a generic claim becomes allowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims limited to species and terminology (claim vs species)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims themselves are never species; a claim may be limited to a single disclosed embodiment (a specific species) or may encompass multiple embodiments (a generic/genus claim). Species refers to the different embodiments of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Species may be independent or related as disclosed. Proper restriction practice depends on this characterization (see MPEP §806.04 and related subsections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction between mutually exclusive species
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction to a single species may be proper when two or more species are claimed and they are mutually exclusive (claims do not overlap in scope).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mutually exclusive: one claim recites limitations disclosed for first species but not second, and vice versa; equivalently, claims must not overlap in scope to require restriction between species. Use MPEP §806.04(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Species must be patentably distinct from each other
rubrics_metrics.description: When requiring restriction among plural species, the examiner should group species considered clearly unpatentable over each other; species must be patentably distinct (not obvious variants and not overlapping in scope) to be separately patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a generic claim is allowable, applicant may claim additional species in the same application per 37 CFR 1.141 and MPEP §806.04. Investigate closely when species are voluntarily presented in separate applications to determine whether double patenting rejection is appropriate (see MPEP §804.01, §804.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic claim filed after issuance of species — obviousness-type double patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: If a generic claim is presented after the issuance of a patent claiming one or more species within the scope of the generic claim, the Office may reject the generic claim on grounds of obviousness-type double patenting when certain common-inventor/assignment conditions exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such rejections may be overcome by filing a terminal disclaimer. Consider 35 U.S.C. 103(c)(2)-(3) joint research agreement exceptions and MPEP §804 guidance; see case law (In re Goodman; In re Braithwaite) for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination vs subcombination distinctness criteria (two-way distinctness and reasons)
rubrics_metrics.description: To support restriction between combination and subcombination inventions, both two-way distinctness and reasons for insisting on restriction are necessary: (A) the combination as claimed does not require the particulars of the subcombination as claimed for patentability (novelty/unobviousness); and (B) the subcombination can be shown to have utility either by itself or in another materially different combination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also require evidence of a serious search burden if restriction not required (separate classification/status/field of search). Examples: (I) subcombination essential to combination -> no restriction; (II) subcombination not essential and has separate utility -> restriction may be proper. Use form paragraph 8.15 and conclude with appropriate form paragraph (e.g., 8.21).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcombinations usable together — distinctness and restriction practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Two or more claimed subcombinations disclosed as usable together in a single combination are usually restrictable when the subcombinations do not overlap in scope and are not obvious variants, and at least one subcombination can be shown separately usable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To support restriction where plural subcombinations are claimed along with a combination including particulars of at least two subcombinations, show two-way distinctness and reasons for restriction (serious search burden evidence). If elected combination is later found allowable, reconsider restriction and rejoin allowable subcombinations per MPEP §821.04. Use form paragraph 8.16 for subcombinations usable together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process and apparatus distinctness criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Process and apparatus for its practice can be shown to be distinct inventions if (A) the process as claimed can be practiced by another materially different apparatus or by hand; or (B) the apparatus as claimed can be used to practice another materially different process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 8.17 for making restriction between process and apparatus claims. A process can be practiced by hand if it can be performed without using any apparatus. If distinctness cannot be shown, restriction between process and apparatus is improper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to demonstrate reasons for insisting on restriction (search burden evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction is proper only when there would be a serious search burden if restriction were not required, evidenced by separate classification, status, or field of search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must document these reasons when imposing restriction; if the applicant provides convincing evidence that suggested separate utility cannot be accomplished, the burden shifts to the examiner to document a viable alternative use or withdraw the requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of restriction and rejoinder when claims are allowable
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon determining that all claims directed to an elected combination invention are allowable, the examiner must reconsider the propriety of the restriction requirement; if combination is allowable in view of patentability of at least one subcombination, withdraw restriction and rejoin the subcombination claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a subcombination is elected and found allowable, nonelected claims requiring all the limitations of the allowable claim will be rejoined in accordance with MPEP §821.04. Applicant is advised that claims presented in a continuation/divisional that are anticipated by or include all limitations of an allowable claim may be subject to provisional double patenting rejections.
